title: From Innovation to Complication: A Case Report and Review on Immune-Related Colitis Induced by ICIs
content: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized cancer therapy by providing durable responses and a favorable safety profile, ushering in a new era in tumor immunotherapy. However, immune-related adverse events (irAEs) remain a significant clinical challenge. Among these, gastrointestinal irAEs, particularly immune-related colitis (ir-colitis), can result in serious complications if not promptly recognized and managed. We report a case of grade 3 ir-colitis induced by sintilimab in a 68-year-old woman receiving treatment for endometrial cancer. The patient developed severe acute diarrhea following ICI administration. Initial antidiarrheal and antimicrobial therapies proved ineffective, and her condition rapidly worsened. A multidisciplinary team (MDT) consisting of gastroenterologists, oncologists, a pathologist, and a clinical pharmacist confirmed the diagnosis of ir-colitis. The discontinuation of sintilimab and initiation of high-dose corticosteroid therapy resulted in marked clinical improvement. In addition to the case report, we provide a comprehensive review of the current literature and clinical guidelines, focusing on risk factors, diagnostic approaches, management strategies, and long-term monitoring of irritable colitis in cancer patients. This case highlights the importance of early recognition, patient education, and MDT collaboration in optimizing outcomes for patients receiving ICIs.
